<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>30.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>EARNINGS PER SHARE - DIVIDENDS</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify; background-color: white">Basic earnings
per share were calculated by dividing net profit attributable to common shareholders of the Bank by the weighted average number of common
shares outstanding during the period.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify; background-color: white">In calculating
the weighted average of outstanding common shares, the number of shares at the beginning of the year is adjusted, if applicable, by the
number of common shares issued or withdrawn during the period, weighted by the number of days those shares have been outstanding. Note
29 provides a breakdown of the changes in the Bank's capital stock.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The calculation of basic earnings
per share is provided in the &ldquo;Earnings per share&rdquo; table of the condensed consolidated interim income Statement. See also
Note 40.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify; text-indent: -0.25in"><U>Dividends
paid and proposed</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Shareholders&rsquo; Meeting held
on April&nbsp;29, 2022, resolved to distribute cash dividends and/or dividends in kind, in this last case, measured at market value for
an amount of 14,187,873 (not restated), representing 22.18 pesos per share, subject to prior authorization from the BCRA which, added
to the dividends still to be paid because they exceeded the abovementioned limit, amounted to 21,016,844 (not restated) and were recorded
in a &ldquo;Reserve for dividends pending authorization from the BCRA&rdquo;. Through Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo; 7719 issued on
March&nbsp;9, 2023, the BCRA established that from April&nbsp;1, 2023 up to December&nbsp;31, 2023, financial institutions which have
the BCRA&rsquo;s authorization, will be allowed to distribute up to 40% of the amount of earnings that should have been distributed if
the &ldquo;Earnings distribution&rdquo; rules&nbsp;had been applied, in six equal, monthly and consecutive installments.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Shareholders&rsquo; Meeting held
on April&nbsp;25, 2023, decided to distribute cash dividends and/or dividends in kind, in this last case, measured at market value for
an amount of 75,040,918 (not restated), representing 117.36 pesos per share, subject to prior authorization from the BCRA. On May&nbsp;12,
2023 the BCRA authorized the dividends distribution, which were paid during the fiscal year ended December&nbsp;31, 2023 according to
the installment schedule.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On September&nbsp;29, 2023, Macro
Agro SAU (formerly known as Comercio Interior SAU) distributed cash dividends for an amount of 440,000 (not restated).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Through Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo;
7984 issued on March&nbsp;21, 2024 the BCRA established that up to December&nbsp;31, 2024, financial institutions which have the BCRA&rsquo;s
authorization will be allowed to distribute up to 60% of the amount of earnings that should have been distributed if the &ldquo;Earnings
distributions&rdquo; rules&nbsp;had been applied, in six equal, monthly and consecutive installments. The amount of each dividend installment
will be paid in homogeneous currency on each payment date.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Shareholders&rsquo; Meeting held
on April&nbsp;12, 2024, approved to distribute cash dividends and/or dividends in kind, in this case measured at market value, for an
amount of 401,735,819,252, representing 628.29 pesos per share, subject to prior BCRA authorization. On May&nbsp;6, 2024, the BCRA authorized
this earnings distribution.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On the other hand, according to Communiqu&eacute;
 &ldquo;A&rdquo; 7997 issued on April&nbsp;30, 2024, the BCRA established that financial institutions which have the BCRA&rsquo;s authorization
will be allowed to distribute earnings in three equal, monthly and consecutive installments. Additionally, financial institutions must
grant the option to each non-resident shareholder to receive their dividends &ndash;totally or partially&ndash; in a single cash installment
as long as those funds are applied directly to the primary subscription of Bonds for the reconstruction of a free Argentina (BOPREAL,
for its acronym in Spanish) in accordance with current exchange regulations.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>31.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>DEPOSIT GUARANTEE INSURANCE</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Law No.&nbsp;24485 and Decree No.&nbsp;540/1995
created the Deposit Guarantee Insurance System, which was featured as a limited, compulsory and onerous system, aimed at covering the
risks of bank deposits, as subsidiary and supplementary to the deposit privilege and protection system established under the Financial
Entities Law. The abovementioned legislation also provided for the incorporation of Sedesa with the exclusive purpose of managing the
Deposit Guarantee Fund (DGF). Sedesa was incorporated in August&nbsp;1995.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">All deposits in pesos and foreign
currency placed in participating entities in the form of checking accounts, savings accounts, certificates of deposits or other forms
of deposit that the BCRA may determine up to the amount of 6,000 which must meet the requirements provided for in Presidential Decree
No.&nbsp;540/1995 and other requirements that the regulatory authority may determine from time to time. Additionally, through Communiqu&eacute;
 &ldquo;A&rdquo; 7985 issued on March&nbsp;27, 2024, the BCRA resolved that, from April&nbsp;1, 2024, the coverage will be up to 25,000.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On the other hand, the BCRA provided
from the exclusion of the guarantee system, among others, of any deposits made by other financial entities, deposits made by persons
related to the Bank and securities deposits.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Translation of Financial Statements originally

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Figures stated in thousands of pesos in constant
currency)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.5in">33.2</TD><TD STYLE="width: 92%">Trusts created using financial assets transferred by the Bank (securitization)</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">The Bank transferred financial assets
(loans) to trusts for the purpose of issuing and selling securities whose collection is guaranteed by the cash flow resulting from such
assets or group of assets. Through this way the funds that were originally used by the Bank to finance the loans are obtained earlier.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">As of March&nbsp;31, 2024 and December&nbsp;31,
2023, considering the latest available accounting information as of the date of issuance of these condensed consolidated interim Financial
Statements, the assets managed through Macro Fiducia SAU (subsidiary) of this type of trusts amounted to 2,636 and 3,997, respectively.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.5in">33.3</TD><TD STYLE="width: 92%">Trusts guaranteeing loans granted by the Bank</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">As it is common in the Argentine banking
market, the Bank requires, in some cases, that the debtors present certain assets or entitlements to receive assets in a trust as a guarantee
for the loans granted. This way, the risk of losses is minimized and access to the security is guaranteed in case of the debtor's non-compliance.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">Trusts usually act as conduits to
collect cash from the debtor&rsquo;s flow of operations and send such cash to the Bank for the payment of the debtor&rsquo;s loans and
thus ensure compliance with the obligations assumed by the trustor and guaranteed through the trust.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">Additionally, other guarantee trusts
manage specific assets, mainly real property.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">Provided there is no non-compliance
or delays by the debtor in the obligations assumed with the beneficiary, the trustee shall not execute the guarantee and all excess amounts
as to the value of the obligations are reimbursed by the trustee to the debtor.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">As of March&nbsp;31, 2024 and December&nbsp;31,
2023, considering the latest available accounting information as of the date of issuance of these condensed consolidated interim Financial
Statements, the assets managed by Banco Macro SA and Macro Fiducia SAU, amounted to 7,284,857 and 1,215,977, respectively.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.5in">33.4</TD><TD STYLE="width: 92%">Trusts in which the Bank acts as Trustee (Management)</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">The Bank, through its subsidiaries,
performs management duties of the corpus assets directly according to the agreements, performing only trustee duties and has no other
interests in the trust.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">In no case shall the trustee be liable
with its own assets or for any obligation deriving from the performance as trustee. Such obligations do not imply any type of indebtedness
or commitment for the trustee and they will be fulfilled only through trust assets. In addition, the trustee will not encumber the corpus
assets or dispose of them beyond the limits established in the related trust agreements. The fees earned by the Bank from its role as
trustee are calculated according to the terms and conditions of the agreements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">Trusts usually manage funds derived
from the activities performed by trustors, for the following main purposes:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 54pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 9.8pt">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">guaranteeing, in favor of the beneficiary
                                            the existence of the resources required to finance and/or pay certain obligations, such as
                                            the payment of amortization installments regarding work or service certificates, and the
                                            payment of invoices and fees stipulated in the related agreements,</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 54pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 9.8pt">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">promoting the production development of the
                                            private economic sector at a provincial level,</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">

of Banco BMA SAU and according to the provisions established by CNV effective as of the approval of General Resolution No.&nbsp;622/2013,
as amended, this company is registered as Comprehensive Settlement and Clearing Agent and Trading Agent (ALyC and AN &ndash; Integral,
as its acronym in Spanish) and as Agent for the Custody of Collective Investment Products of Mutual Funds (AC PIC FCI, for its acronym
in Spanish).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1.25in; text-align: justify">Additionally, the shareholders&rsquo;
equity of such company as of March&nbsp;31, 2024 stated in UVAs amounted to 406,746,112 and exceeds the minimum amount required by such
General Resolution established in 470,350 UVAs, and is integrated with cash balances and equivalents belonging to Banco BMA SAU.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1.25in; text-align: justify">On the other hand, the shareholders&rsquo;
equity of BMA Asset Management SA (formerly known as Ita&uacute; Asset Management SA) as of March&nbsp;31, 2024 stated in UVAs amounted
to 13,208,462 and exceeds the minimum amount required to act as Agent for the Administration of Collective Investment Products of Mutual
Funds, amounting to 150,000 UVAs plus 20,000 UVAs per each additional mutual fund it manages. The minimum statutory guarantee account
required a minimum of 50% of the minimum amount of shareholders&rsquo; equity, which the company paid-in with mutual fund shares.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1.25in; text-align: justify">Similarly, the shareholders&rsquo;
equity of BMA Valores SA (formerly known as Ita&uacute; Valores SA) as of December&nbsp;31, 2023 stated in UVAs amounted to 5,678,211
and exceeds the minimum shareholders&rsquo; equity required, established in 470,350 UVAs, to act as Comprehensive Clearing and Settlement
Agent (ALyC Integral, for its acronym in Spanish) and 163,500 UVAs to act as Comprehensive Mutual Investment Funds Placement and Distribution
Agent, also integrated into mutual funds.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.5in">34.2</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Documents in custody</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">As a general policy, the Bank delivers
for custody to third parties the documentary support of its aged accounting and management operations, i.e. those whose date is prior
to the last fiscal year-end. In compliance with CNV General Resolution No.&nbsp;629 requirements, the Bank has placed (i)&nbsp;the Inventory
Books for fiscal years ended up to and including December&nbsp;31, 2017, and (ii)&nbsp;certain documentation supporting the economic
transactions for fiscal years ended up to and including December&nbsp;31, 2017, under the custody of the following companies: AdeA Administradora
de Archivos SA (warehouse located at Ruta 36, km 31.5, Florencio Varela, Province of Buenos Aires) and ADDOC Administraci&oacute;n de
Documentos SA (warehouse located at Avenida Circunvalaci&oacute;n Agust&iacute;n Tosco with no number, Colectora Sur, between Puente
San Carlos and Puente 60 blocks, Province of C&oacute;rdoba and Avenida Luis Lagomarsino 1750, formerly Ruta 8 Km 51,200, Pilar, Province
of Buenos Aires).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">In addition, the documentary support
in digital format is stored in CD rom, DVD rom and the Bank&rsquo;s own servers.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">On the other hand, Banco BMA SAU safeguards
the documentary support of its aged accounting and management operations, as established by CNV General Resolution No.&nbsp;629, in its
facilities at Victoria Ocampo No.&nbsp;360, 7th floor. Additionally, ADDOC Administraci&oacute;n de documentos SA is entrusted with the
deposit of documentation not included in article 5, paragraph a.3) Section&nbsp;I, Chapter V, Title II of the standards (NT 2013, as
amended), as well as aged documentation, which is placed in its Plant 3 warehouses, located at Ruta 36, km 31,500, Bosques, Florencio
Varela, Province of Buenos Aires.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify"><U>Status</U>: On 10/02/2019, Banco
Macro SA and the liable individuals were notified about the initiation of the proceedings. On 10/31/2019, the Bank and the individuals
subject to summary proceedings filed their defense. On 01/07/2020, the party hearing the summary proceedings considered the defense filed
and deferred the motion to dismiss for lack of capacity to be sued and statute of limitations upon issuing an opinion about the substance
of the case. The administrative terms were suspended due to the social and preventive lockdown declared in the country due to the Covid-19
pandemic (DNU 297/2020), up to and including 11/29/2020. On 11/30/2020, terms were resumed (DNU 876/2020). On 03/02/2021, the passing
of one of the Directors was informed and the lapse of the action against him was requested. In addition, as part of the BCRA summary
proceedings styled &ldquo;File No, 100889/15 &ndash; Banco Macro SA, Summary Proceedings No.&nbsp;1496&rdquo;, Resolution No.&nbsp;2020-132-E-GDEBCRA-SEFYC#BCRA
was issued, whereby penalties were imposed on Banco Macro SA and the parties subject to those proceedings, currently pending before the
CNACAF, Courtroom I (File No.&nbsp;3784/2021). The transactions for which the parties are investigated have already been subject to penalties
in the abovementioned BCRA summary proceedings; therefore, there cannot be simultaneous penalties based on the same subject matter. As
a result, a request was made to prevent the application of all types of penalties to the parties subject to the summary proceedings.
On 08/18/2021, it was resolved to set the case for the production of evidence. On 05/05/2022 the probationary period was closed and the
actions were put to pledge, and on 07/13/2022 it moved to the stage of preparation of the final report. As of the date of issuance of
these condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements, the case is pending resolution.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>NOTES TO THE CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED INTERIM
FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</B>&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>AS OF MARCH&nbsp;31, 2024</B>&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Translation of Financial Statements originally
issued in Spanish &ndash; See Note 44)&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Figures stated in thousands of pesos in constant
currency)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">On April&nbsp;26, 2016, the general
regular shareholders&rsquo; meeting approved the creation of a Global Program for the Issuance of Medium-Term Debt Securities, in accordance
with the provisions of Law No.&nbsp;23576, as amended and further applicable regulations, up to a maximum amount outstanding at any time
during the term of the program of USD 1,000,000,000 (one billion US dollars), or an equal amount in other currencies or power units,
under which it is possible to issue simple corporate bonds, not convertible into shares in one or more classes. Also, on April&nbsp;28,
2017, the General Regular and Special Shareholder&rsquo; Meeting resolved to extend the maximum amount of the abovementioned Global Program
up to USD 1,500,000,000 (one thousand five hundred millions US dollars), and on April&nbsp;27, 2018, the abovementioned Shareholders&rsquo;
Meeting resolved to increase the maximum amount of the Global Program for the Issuance of Corporate Bonds, in face value, from USD 1,500,000,000
to USD 2,500,000,000 or an equal amount in other currencies, as determined by the Board of Directors in due time. Finally, on October&nbsp;20,
2021 due to a Board of Director resolution, the Bank required from the CNV a five-year extension of the abovementioned program, which
was approved by the Regulator through a note issued on December&nbsp;15, 2021.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.75in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">(1)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">On November&nbsp;4, 2016, under the
                                            abovementioned Global Program, the Bank issued Subordinated Resettable Corporate Bonds, class
                                            A, at a fixed rate of 6.750% p.a. until reset date, fully amortizable upon maturity (November&nbsp;4,
                                            2026) for a face value of USD 400,000,000 (four hundred million US dollars), under the terms
                                            and conditions set forth in the pricing supplement dated October&nbsp;21, 2016. Interest
                                            is paid semiannually on May&nbsp;4 and November&nbsp;4 of every year and the reset date was
                                            November&nbsp;4, 2021.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed
consolidated interim Financial Statements, the reset rate was established until the maturity date at 6.643% as a result of the benchmark
reset rate plus 546.3 basis points, according to the abovementioned terms and conditions. As the Bank had not exercised the option to
fully or partially redeem the issuance on the reset date and under the conditions established in the pricing supplement, it was established
up to maturity.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">On the other hand, it could be fully
redeemed, not partially, and only for tax or regulatory purposes. The Bank used the funds derived from such issuance to grant loans in
accordance with BCRA guidelines.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.75in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">(2)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">On May&nbsp;2, 2022, under the abovementioned
                                            Global Program, the Bank issued Class&nbsp;E non-subordinated simple corporate bonds not
                                            convertible into shares, for a face value of USD 17,000,000 at a fixed rate of 1.45%, fully
                                            amortizable upon maturity (May&nbsp;2, 2024), under the terms and conditions set forth in
                                            the price supplement dated April&nbsp;21, 2022. Interest is paid quarterly on August&nbsp;2,
                                            2022, November&nbsp;2, 2022, February&nbsp;2, 2023, May&nbsp;2, 2023, August&nbsp;2, 2023,
                                            November&nbsp;2, 2023, February&nbsp;2, 2024, and May&nbsp;2, 2024.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">At any time, according to the current
regulations, particularly the BCRA&rsquo;s foreign exchange regulations, the Bank may opt to redeem Class&nbsp;E Corporate Bonds in full,
not partially, at a price equal to (a)&nbsp;102% of the outstanding principal if the Bank decides to make the redemption from the date
of issuance and settlement through the term of 9 months therefrom, including the last business day; (b)&nbsp;101% of outstanding principal
if the Bank decides to make the redemption within the term starting 9 months after the date of issuance and settlement until the Class&nbsp;E
maturity date, in all cases, along with the additional amount and accrued and unpaid interest, excluding the redemption date.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">On May&nbsp;2, 2024, the whole issuance
of this series and the interest service corresponding to the period between February&nbsp;2, 2024, date included, and May&nbsp;2, 2024
were paid off.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

                                            abovementioned Global Program, the Bank issued Class&nbsp;F corporate bonds for a face value
                                            of USD 53,000,000 (fifty-three million US dollars) at a fixed rate of 5%, fully amortizable
                                            upon maturity (October&nbsp;31, 2024), under the terms and conditions set forth in the price
                                            supplement dated October&nbsp;24, 2023. Interest is paid semiannually on April&nbsp;30, 2024,
                                            and at the expiration date.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">At any time, according to the current
regulations, particularly the BCRA&rsquo;s foreign exchange regulations, the Bank may opt to redeem Class&nbsp;F corporate bonds in full,
but not partially, at a price equal to (a)&nbsp;102% of the outstanding principal if the Bank decides to redeem the bonds between the
date of issuance and settlement date through the term of 9 months therefrom, including the last business day; (b)&nbsp;101% of outstanding
principal if the Bank decides to redeem them within the term starting 9 months after the date of issuance and settlement through Class&nbsp;F
corporate bonds maturity date; in any case, along with the additional amounts and accrued and unpaid interest, excluding the redemption
date.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">Before merging with and into the Bank,
Banco Privado de Inversiones SA (BPI) had a pending class action styled &ldquo;Adecua v, Banco Privado de Inversiones on ordinary proceedings&rdquo;,
File No.&nbsp;19073/2007, pending with National Commercial Court No.&nbsp;3, Clerk&rsquo;s Office No.&nbsp;5, whereby it was required
to reimburse to its clients the life insurance amounts overcharged to amounts payable as well as to reduce the amounts charged in this
regard in the future; this legal proceeding was concluded upon the abovementioned merger because BPI complied in full with the terms
of the court-approved agreement reached with Adecua before answering the complaint. However, in March&nbsp;2013, when BPI had already
been merged with and into the Bank, the trial court resolved to amend the terms of the agreement and ordered the reimbursement of amounts
of money to a larger number of clients as compared to the number arising from the terms approved by the court in due time. Such resolution
was appealed by the Bank as BPI&rsquo;s surviving company. The appeal was dismissed by the Court of Appeals, which abrogated both the
trial court decision and the court-approved agreement, thus ordering the Bank to answer the complaint. This gave rise to the filing of
an extraordinary appeal against such decision as well as the subsequent filing of a complaint for the extraordinary appeal denied. On
May&nbsp;5, 2021, the Bank was notified of the dismissal of the complaint appeal, ordering the return of the main process to the National
Court of Appeals for continuing with the proceedings, who also submitted them to the trial court, which received them on 09/27/2021 and
were requested as effectum vivendi in proceedings &ldquo;Estado Nacional &ndash; Ministerio Producci&oacute;n de la Naci&oacute;n c/
Asociaci&oacute;n de Defensa de los Consumidores y Usuarios de la R.A y otros s/Ordinario&rdquo; (File No.&nbsp;6757/2013), in which
the Bank is not a party, by the national commercial court No.&nbsp;6, clerk&rsquo;s office No.&nbsp;11, where, as of the date of issuance
of these condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements, they are still filed.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">Moreover, the Bank is subject to another
collective action for the same purpose, currently pending with National Commercial Court No.&nbsp;7, Clerk&rsquo;s Office No.&nbsp;13,
styled Uni&oacute;n de Usuarios y Consumidores v, Nuevo Banco Bisel on ordinary proceedings, File No.&nbsp;44704/2008.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">There are also other class actions
initiated by consumer protection associations in relation to the collection of certain commissions and/or financial charges or practices
and certain withholdings made by the Bank to individuals as CABA stamp tax withholding agent.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

currency)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">Additionally, profits may only be distributed
to the extent that the financial institution has positive results, after deducting, on a non-accounting basis, from retained earnings
and the optional reserves for the future distribution of profits, (i)&nbsp;the amounts of the legal and other earnings reserves which
are mandatory, (ii)&nbsp;all debit amounts of each one of the accounting items recognized in &ldquo;Other Comprehensive Income&rdquo;,
(iii)&nbsp;income from the revaluation of property, plant and equipment, intangible assets and investment property, (iv)&nbsp;the positive
net difference between the amortized cost and the fair value of government debt instruments and/or monetary regulation instruments issued
by the BCRA for those instruments recognized at amortized cost, (v)&nbsp;the adjustments identified by the Superintendence of Financial
and Exchange Entities of the BCRA or by the independent external auditor and that have not been recognized in the accounting records
and (vi)&nbsp;certain franchises granted by the BCRA. Moreover, no profit distributions shall be made out of the profit originated as
a result of the first-time application of the IFRS, for which a normative reserve was created, and its balance as of March&nbsp;31, 2024
was 101,052,679 (nominal value: 3,475,669).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">The Bank must verify that, after completion
of the earning distribution, a capital maintenance margin equal to 3.5% of risk-weighted assets is kept, apart from the minimum capital
required by law, to be integrated by Tier 1 (COn1) ordinary capital, net of deductible items (CDCOn1).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">According to Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo;
7984, the BCRA established that up to December&nbsp;31, 2024, financial institutions which have the prior BCRA&rsquo;s authorization
will be allowed to distribute earnings up to 60% of the amount that would have corresponded in six equal, monthly and consecutive installments.
Moreover, the BCRA established that the calculation of the items to determine the distributable earnings, as well as the amount of the
installments, must be stated in constant currency as of the date of the meeting and the date of payment of each installment, as applicable.
Subsequently, through Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo; 7997, the BCRA established that financial institutions that resolve or have resolved
to distribute earnings within the framework of what is expected by the Communiqu&eacute; &quot;A&rdquo; 7984, will be allowed to distribute
earnings in three equal, monthly and consecutive installments up to the related amount in accordance with the abovementioned Communiqu&eacute;.
Such Communiqu&eacute; also established that financial institutions must grant the option to each non-resident shareholder to receive
their dividends &ndash;totally or partially&ndash; in a single cash installment as long as those funds are applied directly to the primary
subscription of Bonds for the reconstruction of a free Argentina (BOPREAL, for its acronym in Spanish) in accordance with current exchange
regulations.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>42.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>CHANGES IN THE ARGENTINE MACROECONOMIC
                                            ENVIRONMENT AND FINANCIAL AND CAPITAL MARKETS</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">In the last years, the argentine financial
market has observed a prolonged period of volatility in the market prices of public and private financial instruments, including a high
level of country risk, an increase in the official exchange rate between the argentine peso and the US dollar, an increase in interest
rates and a significant acceleration of the inflation rate (see Note 3. section &quot;unit of measurement&quot;).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Particularly, related to the price
of the US dollar, since the end of 2019 the gap between the official price of the US dollar -used mainly for foreign trade- and alternative
market values began to widen significantly, having reached maximum peaks close to 200%. As of the date of issuance of these condensed
consolidated interim Financial Statements, the aforementioned gap amounts to approximately 38%.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Regarding the administration of the
national public debt, a restructuring process has been observed, including various voluntary exchanges and agreements reached regarding
debts with the Paris Club and the International Monetary Fund.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">In this context, on December&nbsp;10,
2023, the new authorities of the argentine national government took office and issued a series of emergency measures. Among the main
objectives pursued, among other relevant issues, are a regulatory flexibility in economic matters, reduction of the fiscal deficit mainly
through a reduction in spending, including reduction of different types of subsidies. Likewise, there was a devaluation of the argentine
peso close to 55% against to the US dollar (increasing the US dollar price from 366.50 pesos to 799.95 pesos on December&nbsp;13, 2023),
which has generated an acceleration of the inflation rate, with interannual inflation measured from the national CPI published by INDEC
being 289.4% at the date of issue of these condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The comprehensive program pursued
by the new national government includes reforms in the economy, justice, foreign relations, infrastructure and others. On December&nbsp;20,
2023, through Decree of Necessity and Urgency No.&nbsp;70/2023, a significant number of reforms were established, regarding which different
actors presented various protections or unconstitutionality requests to Justice to stop their application. On the other hand, as of the
date of issuance of these condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements, a bill is under parliamentary treatment and include among
its points, delegation of powers to the Executive Branch, tax, labor and social security reforms, among others.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">In addition, the local and international
macroeconomic context generates certain degree of uncertainty regarding its future progress, considering the level of the global economic
recovery.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Therefore, the Bank&rsquo;s Management
permanently monitors any changes in the abovementioned situations, to determine the possible actions to adopt and to identify the possible
impact on its financial situation that may need to be reflected in the future Financial Statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>43.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>EVENTS AFTER REPORTING PERIOD</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">No other significant events occurred
between the end of the period and the issuance of these condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements that may materially affect
the financial position or the profit and loss of the period, not disclosed in these condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>1.</B></TD><TD><B>CORPORATE INFORMATION</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Banco Macro SA (hereinafter, the &ldquo;Bank&rdquo;)
is a business corporation (<I>sociedad an&oacute;nima</I>) organized in the Argentine Republic that offers traditional banking products
and services to companies, including those companies operating in regional economies as well as to individuals, thus strengthening its
goal to be a multiservice bank. In addition, the Bank performs certain transactions through its subsidiaries Macro Bank Limited (a company
organized under the laws of Bahamas), Macro Securities SAU, Macro Fiducia SAU, Macro Fondos SGFCISA, Argenpay SAU and Fintech SGR.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Macro Compa&ntilde;&iacute;a Financiera
SA was created in 1977 as a non-banking financial institution. In May&nbsp;1988, it received the authorization to operate as a commercial
bank and was incorporated as Banco Macro SA. Subsequently, as a result of the merger process with other entities, it adopted other names
(among them, Banco Macro Bansud SA) and since August&nbsp;2006, Banco Macro SA.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank&rsquo;s shares are publicly
listed on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos (BYMA) since November&nbsp;1994 and as from March&nbsp;24, 2006, they are listed on the New York
Stock Exchange (NYSE). Additionally, on October&nbsp;15, 2015 they were authorized to be listed on the Mercado Abierto Electr&oacute;nico
SA (MAE).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Since 1994, Banco Macro SA&rsquo;s
market strategy has mainly focused on the regional areas outside the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires (CABA, for its acronym in Spanish).
Following this strategy, in 1996, Banco Macro SA started the process to acquire entities and assets and liabilities during the privatization
of provincial and other banks.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">In 2001, 2004, 2006 and 2010, the Bank
acquired the control of Banco Bansud SA, Nuevo Banco Suqu&iacute;a SA, Nuevo Banco Bisel SA and Banco Privado de Inversiones SA, respectively.
Such entities merged with and into Banco Macro SA in December&nbsp;2003, October&nbsp;2007, August&nbsp;2009 and December&nbsp;2013, respectively.
During the fiscal year 2006, the Bank acquired control over Banco del Tucum&aacute;n SA, which was merged with Banco Macro SA in October&nbsp;2019.
Additionally, on October&nbsp;1, 2021, the Bank acquired the control of Fintech SGR that, as explained in Note 3 to the consolidated Financial
Statements as of December&nbsp;31, 2023, already issued, this is a structured entity in which the Bank has control.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">During 2023, 2022, 2021 and 2020 the
Bank in conjunction with other entities of the argentine financial system made contributions in the company Play Digital SA for a total
amount of 977,225 (not restated), reaching an equity interest of 9.1886%. See also Note 1 to the condensed consolidated interim Financial
Statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On May&nbsp;18, 2023, Banco Macro SA
acquired 100% of Macro Agro SAU (formerly known as Comercio Interior SAU) capital stock at USD 5,218,800 payable with the proceeds of
this company&rsquo;s dividends. The main purpose of this company is grain brokerage. For further information see also Note 9.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Additionally, on November&nbsp;2, 2023,
the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Argentina (BCRA, for its acronym in Spanish), authorized the acquisition by Banco Macro
SA of 100% of the capital stock of Banco Ita&uacute; Argentina SA,&nbsp;Ita&uacute; Asset Management SA and Ita&uacute; Valores SA. For
further information see also Note 1 to the condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On May&nbsp;22, 2024, the Board of
Directors approved the issuance of these condensed separate interim Financial Statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">

<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>3.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>BASIS FOR THE PREPARATION OF THESE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS AND APPLICABLE ACCOUNTING STANDARDS</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Applicable Accounting Standards</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">These condensed separate interim Financial
Statements of the Bank were prepared in accordance with the accounting framework established by the BCRA, in its Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo;
6114 as supplemented. Except for the exceptions established by the BCRA, which are explained in the following paragraph, such framework
is based on International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB) and adopted
by the Argentine Federation of Professionals Councils in Economic Sciences (FACPCE, for its acronym in Spanish). The abovementioned international
standards include the IFRS, the International Accounting Standards (IAS) and the interpretations developed by the IFRS Interpretations
Committee (IFRIC) or former IFRIC (SIC).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The transitory exceptions and regulatory
guidelines established by BCRA to the application of effective IFRS, that affect the preparation of these condensed separate interim Financial
Statements are as follows:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">a)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">According to Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo; 6114, as supplemented, and in the convergence process through
IFRS, the BCRA established that since fiscal years beginning on or after January&nbsp;1, 2020, financial institutions defined as &ldquo;Group
A&rdquo; by BCRA rules, in which the Bank is included, begin to apply section 5.5 &ldquo;Impairment&rdquo; of the IFRS 9 &ldquo;Financial
Instruments&rdquo; (sections B5.5.1 to B5.5.55), except for the temporary exclusion for the debt securities of the non-financial public
sector established by BCRA Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo; 6847. As of the date of issuance of these condensed separate interim Financial
Statements, the Bank is in the process of quantifying the effect of the full application of the abovementioned standard.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">b)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Through Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A 7014 dated May&nbsp;14, 2020, the BCRA established for financial institutions
that received debt securities of the public sector in a swap transaction, they must be initially recognized at their carrying amount as
of the date of the swap transaction, without assessing if they qualify or not for derecognition under IFRS 9 standards and as a consequence,
do not eventually recognize the new instruments at the market value as provided by such IFRS (see Note 9 to the condensed consolidated
interim Financial Statements).</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">If IFRS 9 had applied, and according
an estimation calculated by the Bank, the Statement of income of the period ended March&nbsp;31, 2024, would have recorded a decrease
in &ldquo;Other operating income&rdquo; for an amount of 2,012,244. On the other hand, an increase in &ldquo;Loss on net monetary position&rdquo;
for an amount of 1,554,435 and a decrease in &ldquo;Net gain from measurement of financial instruments at fair value through profit or
loss&rdquo; for an amount of 215,304, and as a counterpart an increase in &ldquo;Other comprehensive income&rdquo; for that period. In
addition, it would have been recorded in the Statement of income of the period ended March&nbsp;31, 2023 a decrease in &ldquo;Other operating
income&rdquo; for an amount of 4,654,240. On the other hand, a decrease in &ldquo;Loss on net monetary position&rdquo; for an amount of
1,407,955 and an increase in &ldquo;Net gain from measurement of financial instruments at fair value through profit or loss&rdquo; for
an amount of 6,429,045, and as a counterpart an increase in &ldquo;Other comprehensive income&rdquo; for that period. These changes would
not have resulted into modifications to the total shareholder equity as of that date nor the total comprehensive income of the three-month
periods ended March&nbsp;31, 2024 and 2023.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Applicable Accounting Policies</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Except for what was mentioned in the
previous paragraphs, the accounting policies applied by the Bank comply with the IFRS as currently approved and are applicable to the
preparation of these condensed separate interim Financial Statements in accordance with the IFRS as adopted by the BCRA through Communiqu&eacute;
 &ldquo;A&rdquo; 7899. Generally, the BCRA does not allow the anticipated application of any IFRS, unless otherwise expressly stated.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Note 3 to the consolidated Financial
Statements as of December&nbsp;31, 2023, already issued presents further detailed descriptions of the basis for the presentation of such
Financial Statements and the main accounting policies used and the relevant information of the subsidiaries. All that is explained therein
shall apply to these condensed separate interim Financial Statements, except for the goodwill generated by the business combination, as
mentioned in Note 9, which according to BCRA Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo; 6618, in the condensed separate interim Financial Statements,
is included in the net investment of the subsidiary.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Going concern</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank&rsquo;s Management has made
an assessment of its ability to continue as a going concern and is satisfied that it has the resources to continue in business for the
foreseeable future. Furthermore, management is not aware of any material uncertainties that may cast significant doubt on the Bank&rsquo;s
ability to continue as a going concern. Therefore, these condensed separate interim Financial Statements continue to be prepared on the
going concern basis.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Subsidiaries</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">As mentioned in Note 1, the Bank performs
certain transactions through its subsidiaries.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Subsidiaries are all the entities controlled
by the Bank. An entity controls another entity when it is exposed, or has rights, to variable returns from its continuing involvement
with such other entity and has the ability to use its power to direct the operating and financing policies of such other entity, to affect
the amounts of such returns.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">As provided under IAS 27 &ldquo;Consolidated
and Separate Financial Statements&rdquo;, investments in subsidiaries were accounted for using the &ldquo;equity method&rdquo;, established
in IAS 28 &ldquo;Investments in associates and joint ventures&rdquo;. When using this method, investments are initially recognized at
cost, and such amount increases or decreases to recognize investor&rsquo;s interest in profit and loss of the entity after the date of
acquisition or creation.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Shares in profit and loss of subsidiaries
and associates are recognized under &ldquo;Income / (loss) from subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures&rdquo; in the condensed separate
interim statement of income. Ownership interest in other comprehensive income of subsidiaries is accounted for under &ldquo;Income / (loss)
of the period from interest in other comprehensive income of subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures accounted for using the participation
method&rdquo;, in the condensed separate interim statement of other comprehensive income.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Transcription into books</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">As of the date of issuance of these
condensed separate interim Financial Statements, they are in the process of being transcribed into the Financial Statements book (&ldquo;Libro
Balance&rdquo;) of Banco Macro SA.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><B><U>New standards adopted</U></B></P>

<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>4.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>CONTINGENT TRANSACTIONS</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">In order to meet specific financial
needs of customers, the Bank&rsquo;s credit policy also includes, among others, the granting of guarantees, securities, bonds, letters
of credit and documentary credits. The Bank is also exposed to overdrafts and unused agreed credits on credit cards of the Bank. Since
they imply a contingent obligation for the Bank, they expose the Bank to credit risks other than those recognized in the Statement of
financial position and, therefore, they are an integral part of the total risk of the Bank.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>NOTES TO THE CONDENSED SEPARATE INTERIM FINANCIAL
STATEMENTS</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>AS OF MARCH&nbsp;31, 2024</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Translation of Financial Statements originally
issued in Spanish &ndash; See Note 41)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Figures stated in thousands of pesos in constant
currency)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>7.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>LOSS ALLOWANCE FOR EXPECTED CREDIT LOSSES ON CREDIT EXPOSURES NOT MEASURED AT FAIR VALUE THROUGH PROFIT
OR LOSS</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank recognizes a loss allowance
for expected credit losses on all credit exposures not measured at fair value through profit or loss, like debt instruments measured at
amortized cost, debt instruments measured at fair value through other comprehensive income, loan commitments and financial guarantee contracts
(not measured at fair value through profit or loss), contract assets and lease receivables.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Note 8 discloses financial assets measured
at fair value on a recurring basis and financial assets not recognized at fair value. This classification is made pursuant to the expressed
in Note 3 &ldquo;Basis for the preparation of these Financial Statements and applicable accounting standards&rdquo;. Additionally, Note
8 explains the information related to the valuation process.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Moreover, considering the temporary
exclusion established by BCRA mentioned in Note 3 &ldquo;Applicable accounting standards&rdquo; the Bank applies the impairment requirements
for the recognition and measurement of a loss allowance for financial assets measured at amortized cost or at fair value through other
comprehensive income, except for public sector exposures. In addition, the Bank applies the impairment requirements for guarantees granted,
undrawn commitments of credit cards and checking accounts, letter of credits, which are not recognized in the condensed consolidated interim
statement of financial position.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">For the purpose of assessing the Bank&rsquo;s
credit risk exposure and identifying material credit risk concentration, disclosures regarding credit risk of financial assets and items
not recognized in the statement of financial position are as follows.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.5in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in">(1)</TD><TD>As explained in Note 3, ECL is not calculated to public sector exposures.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">As explained in Note 45.1.3 to the consolidated
Financial Statements as of December&nbsp;31, 2023, already issued, &ldquo;Additional Forward-looking allowances based on expert credit
judgment&rdquo;, section &ldquo;Adjustment for expectations of increased risk due to the change in economic policy&rdquo;, the Bank resolved
to carry out an adjustment with a prospective vision as a consequence of estimating an incremental effect in the forecasts determined
by ECL for the purposes of covering a scenario of uncertainty regarding the impacts that could originate from the change in the economic
policy regime, the implementation of a program to adjust imbalances macroeconomics and an inflation stabilization plan. As of March&nbsp;31,
2024 and December&nbsp;31, 2023, said adjustment was estimated at 10,089,134 and 16,645,255, respectively, as explained in the section
 &quot;Adjustment for uncertainty about conditions of accessing loans to MIPYMES&quot; of the aforementioned note.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">The following table shows the credit
quality and the carrying amount of credit risk, based on the Bank&rsquo;s credit risk rating system, the probability of default (PD) and
the year-end stage classification, taking into account what was mentioned in the previous paragraph. The amounts are presented gross of
the impairment allowances.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">The criterion
used to calculate ECL of Financial Trusts and Corporate Bonds is based on the rating granted by risk rating agencies to each debt security
type making up the financial trusts or each corporate bond series, respectively. This means that the factor to be used will vary depending
on the debt securities holdings (A or B). The EAD is assumed to be equal to the outstanding balance.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>NOTES TO THE CONDENSED SEPARATE INTERIM FINANCIAL
STATEMENTS</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>AS OF MARCH&nbsp;31, 2024</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Translation of Financial Statements originally
issued in Spanish &ndash; See Note 41)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Figures stated in thousands of pesos in constant
currency)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>8.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>FAIR VALUE QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Note 10 to the condensed consolidated
interim Financial Statements describes the methods and assumptions used to determine the fair value, both of the financial instruments
recognized at fair value as of those not accounted for at such fair value in these condensed separate interim Financial Statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">In addition, the Bank discloses the
relevant information as to instruments included in Level 3 of the fair value hierarchy.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Even though the Bank&rsquo;s Management
has used its best judgment to estimate the fair values of its financial instruments, any technique to perform such estimate implies certain
inherent fragility level.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in"><U>Fair value hierarchy</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank uses the following hierarchy
to determine and disclose the fair value of financial instruments, according to the valuation technique applied:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 10.35pt">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Level 1: quoted prices (unadjusted) observable in active markets that the Bank accesses to at the measurement
day for identical assets or liabilities. The Bank considers markets as active only if there are sufficient trading activities with respect
to the volume and liquidity of the identical assets or liabilities and when there are binding and exercisable price quotes available at
each period or fiscal year, as applicable.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 10.35pt">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Level 2: Valuation techniques for which the data and variables having a significant impact on the determination
of the fair value recognized or disclosed are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly. Such inputs include
quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets, quoted prices for identical instruments in inactive markets and observable
inputs other than quoted prices, such as interest rates and yield curves, implied volatilities, and credit spreads. In addition, adjustments
to level 2 inputs may be required for the condition or location of the asset or the extent to which it relates to items that are comparable
to the valued instrument. However, if such adjustments are based on unobservable inputs that are significant to the entire measurement,
the Bank will classify the instruments as Level 3.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 10.35pt">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Level 3: Valuation techniques for which the data and variables having a significant impact on the determination
of the fair value recognized or disclosed are not based on observable market information.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The following tables show the hierarchy
in the Bank&rsquo;s financial asset and liability at fair value measurement, as of March&nbsp;31, 2024 and December&nbsp;31, 2023:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>NOTES TO THE CONDENSED SEPARATE INTERIM FINANCIAL
STATEMENTS</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>AS OF MARCH&nbsp;31, 2024</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Translation of Financial Statements originally
issued in Spanish &ndash; See Note 41)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Figures stated in thousands of pesos in constant
currency)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify; background-color: white">Note 10 to
the condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements, details the valuation techniques and significant unobservable inputs used in
the valuation of assets at Level 3.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify; background-color: white"><U>Changes
in fair value levels</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank monitors the availability
of information in the market to evaluate the classification of financial instruments into the fair value hierarchy as well as the resulting
determination of transfers between levels 1, 2 and 3 at each period end.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Except for the foregoing, as of March&nbsp;31,
2024 and December&nbsp;31, 2023, the Bank has not recognized any transfers between levels 1, 2 and 3.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

SA and Ita&uacute; Valores SA.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>12.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>RELATED PARTIES</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">A related party is a person or entity
that is related to the Bank:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 17.45pt; text-align: left"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 10pt">-</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 10pt">has control or joint control of
the Bank;</FONT></TD>
</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 17.45pt; text-align: left"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 10pt">-</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 10pt">has significant influence over
the Bank;</FONT></TD>
</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 17.45pt; text-align: left"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 10pt">-</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 10pt">is a member of the key management
personnel of the Bank or of a parent of the Bank;</FONT></TD>
</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 17.45pt; text-align: left"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 10pt">-</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 10pt">members of the same group;</FONT></TD>
</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 17.45pt; text-align: left"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 10pt">-</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 10pt">one entity is an associate (or
an associate of a member of a group of which the other entity is a member).</FONT></TD>
</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Key management personnel are those
persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Bank, directly or indirectly.
The Bank considers as key management personnel, for the purposes of IAS 24, the members of the Board of Directors and the senior management
members of the Risk Management Committee, the Assets and Liabilities Committee and the Senior Credit Committee.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>
